correctness.rationale: Lassak's reduction allows restriction to inscribed centrally symmetric parallelograms. The package's three side-separation cases exhaust such parallelograms in the regular decagon up to dihedral symmetry and exchange of generators. The same-side and adjacent-side cases give lower bounds at least \(2\varphi\) and \(\varphi\), respectively, both above the target. In the remaining separated-by-one-side case, the displayed gauge coordinates \(A/E,B/E,C/E\), monotonicities, crossing locations, and residual factorizations correctly prove \(\max\{A,B,C\}/E\ge(3\sqrt5-1)/4\). An independent dense numerical sweep over all side pairs and side parameters found the same minimum at a vertex/midpoint configuration. Lassak's coordinate-axis construction gives the matching upper bound, so the exact distance follows.
residual_risks: The independent numerical sweep is only corroborative; the exact lower bound rests on the complete symbolic case split.

originality.rationale: Lassak's open full article explicitly proves exact values only for the \(8j\) and \(8j+4\) families, gives an upper bound for \(8j+2\), and then conjectures equality for that family. At \(j=1\) this is exactly the decagon constant proved here. Targeted current searches for the decagon, the exact radical, and the Lassak \(8j+2\) conjecture found no later proof, and Resultary returned the assigned record as the exact hit. The lower bound is therefore a genuine resolution of the first open case rather than a specialization of a proved general theorem.
residual_risks: A weakly indexed later solution of the \(j=1\) case could exist, but none was found in targeted current searches.
